ai_language: "I've reduced it from 9,000 heads to about 5,000, because I need less heads" — with Agentforce AI agents now handling ~50% of customer interactions. (CEO Marc Benioff)
excerpt: Benioff said Salesforce cut its customer-support headcount from ~9,000 to ~5,000 (~4,000 roles) in 2025 as Agentforce AI agents took over about half of support interactions.

ai_language: "The companies that will win in the AI era will be those with focus, urgency, and the discipline to continuously shift investment toward the areas where demand and long-term value creation are strongest." (CEO Chuck Robbins, memo)
excerpt: Cisco cut ~5,600 jobs (7%) in Aug 2024 to reallocate investment toward AI and cybersecurity growth areas. Framed as an AI-driven investment shift rather than AI directly replacing workers.

ai_language: "With the planned transformation program, we are intensifying the shift of investments to strategic growth areas, above all Business AI." (CEO Christian Klein)
excerpt: SAP announced a restructuring affecting 8,000 roles to refocus on Business AI. Mostly voluntary buyouts/re-skilling — SAP said total headcount would stay similar by year-end, so this is a restructuring toward AI rather than a net layoff.

ai_language: CEO Sasan Goodarzi's memo framed the reorganization around increasing investment in AI and generative AI ("Intuit Assist"), stating: "We do not do layoffs to cut costs, and that remains true in this case."
excerpt: Intuit laid off 1,800 (10%) in a reorganization to accelerate AI investment, while planning to rehire ~1,800 in AI/engineering roles. Mixed rationale — some cuts were performance-based; AI is the strategic framing.

ai_language: "Companies everywhere are reimagining how work gets done, and the increasing demand for AI has the potential to drive a new era of growth for Workday." (CEO Carl Eschenbach)
excerpt: Workday cut 1,750 jobs (8.5%), with the CEO citing AI demand and reallocation toward AI investment as the rationale for the restructuring.

ai_language: "It is doing the equivalent work of 700 full-time agents." (Klarna, on its OpenAI-powered AI assistant)
excerpt: Klarna said its AI assistant handles two-thirds of customer-service chats and does the work equivalent to 700 full-time agents. Caveat: this is a work-equivalence figure, not a discrete 700-person termination; the agents were largely outsourced.

ai_language: "AI flattens our hiring curve, and helps us innovate from idea to product faster. It streamlines go-to-market, improves customer outcomes, and drives efficiencies across both the front and back office." (CEO George Kurtz, staff memo)
excerpt: CrowdStrike cut 500 jobs (~5% of workforce), with CEO George Kurtz's memo framing AI as a force multiplier that flattens the company's hiring curve.

ai_language: "the AI era of computing has finally arrived" — CEO Drew Houston said the company needs "a different mix of skill sets, particularly in AI and early-stage product development."
excerpt: Dropbox laid off 500 employees (16% of staff), with CEO Drew Houston citing slowing growth and a strategic pivot to AI as the rationale.

ai_language: Chegg attributed the cuts to the "new realities of AI" — generative AI's rapid adoption among students (ChatGPT) and traffic lost to Google's AI search summaries.
excerpt: Chegg laid off 388 employees (~45% of staff), its fourth round since mid-2024, citing collapsing demand as students shifted to ChatGPT and AI search summaries.

ai_language: "We had to layoff 90% of our support team because of this AI chatbot. Tough? Yes. Necessary? Absolutely." (CEO Suumit Shah)
excerpt: Dukaan's CEO said the company replaced 90% of its customer-support team (~23 people) with an AI chatbot named 'Lina,' which he publicized in July 2023.
